title: Read a backslash-continued invocation as one command in the docs CLI-shape scan
action: The docs scanner in hooks/cli_shape.rs walks text.lines() one at a time inside a fenced block, so a documented invocation continued with a trailing backslash is only ever checked as its FIRST physical line. Every flag written on a continuation then reports as MISSING against an example that is already correct — a refusal the reader cannot act on. Join continued lines before checking, exactly as the shell does: drop the trailing backslash, join with one space, and reset the accumulator at a fence boundary. Add a test that a correct multi-line invocation passes and a genuinely malformed one still fails, so the fix cannot become a way to smuggle bad spellings past the guard.

truths: A fenced invocation continued with a trailing backslash is checked as ONE joined command, not as its first line.
The join matches the shell: the backslash is dropped and one space joins the parts.
A fence boundary resets the accumulator, so a dangling continuation never leaks into the next block.
A genuinely malformed multi-line invocation is STILL refused — the fix must not become a way past the guard, and a test proves it.
The three-line bee decisions log example in docs/product-description/memory/decisions.md stops being reported, because it was always correct.
The scan's checked-count assertion stays non-vacuous.

acceptance: A backslash-continued example is checked whole; a malformed one still refuses; fence boundaries reset the join; the cli_shape suite is green and the corpus count stays non-vacuous.
